audit.why: Emerald+ 48.11% over 1268 games — the largest sample in this slice and a genuine losing lane, which the EVEN / 6-10 labels slightly flatter but the level chart (Sion at 1, 4-5 and late) reflects honestly.

Sion takes level 1 on ranged poke, Rumble takes 2 and 6, Sion takes 4-5 behind Soul Furnace and everything late. The chart is right. Sion is the most immobile champion in the game, which is why Rumble's level 6 window is genuine and why the side lane never fully belongs to either.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 1 spike is built on a false mechanic — that Roar of the Slayer shreds Rumble's magic resist — and the 4-5 spike describes Soul Furnace as pure absorption.
audit.why: Roar of the Slayer reduces Armor, per Riot's description. Rumble deals magic damage almost exclusively, so the shred is close to irrelevant to him and the real level-1 threat is the poke itself, especially fired through a minion, which knocks the minion back and hits everyone behind it. Soul Furnace is also not just a shield: 'Sion shields himself and can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby' with max-health scaling — a Sion holding his shield is holding a damage button, which changes when you choose to be next to him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup tells the player three times to 'double-cast Electro-Harpoon to interrupt his Q charge'. Electro-Harpoon is a slow. A slow does not interrupt a charge. Following this advice means standing in the Decimating Smash arc while throwing harpoons and eating the knockup.
audit.why: Rumble's E is described by Riot as launching a harpoon that damages, slows Move Speed and reduces Magic Resist — the kit's only flags on it are projectile and slow. There is no interrupt, no knockback and no cast-stop anywhere in Rumble's kit. Decimating Smash's only counterplay from Rumble is positional: leave the arc. Separately, Roar of the Slayer knocks back minions and monsters only, not champions, and the text says it knocks Rumble back.
audit.corrected: Corrected in wants.you[1], whys[0], whys[2], dosFull[0].d, the Key Ability Interactions report line and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in a matchup whose entire structure is 'trade around Decimating Smash'.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11s, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8s, Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60s. The Q number in particular reframes the advice — at 10s it comes back fast enough that the answer has to be positional rather than a wait.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d rewritten with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Itemization line says to rush anti-heal 'early — his healing fights your pattern'. Sion has no lane sustain to fight.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags Sion for needs-antiheal, but the source it names is Glory in Death, his passive: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate... His attacks become very rapid, heal him.' That is a post-death state, not lane sustain. Grievous Wounds in this matchup is for the zombie, which means the timing advice is wrong even though the item is right — and the zombie is exactly when a Rumble who just committed everything is most likely to die.
audit.corrected: The Itemization report line now points Grievous Wounds at Glory in Death.

edits.before: Sion's E (Roar of the Slayer) shreds your Scrap Shield's magic resist and pokes you for free before you have Heat to trade back.
edits.after: Roar of the Slayer cuts armour, not magic resist, so it barely dents you — the free poke comes from him firing it through a minion.

edits.before: Sion's W shield absorbs your entire Flamespitter tick before he charges Q through it — trading into a fully-charged W costs you the exchange every time.
edits.after: Soul Furnace absorbs your Flamespitter, and after 3 seconds he can pop it for max-health magic damage — a held shield is a loaded button, not just armour.

edits.before: Double-cast Electro-Harpoon the moment he starts winding up his Q to interrupt his charge
edits.after: Step out of the Decimating Smash arc — Electro-Harpoon is a slow, and slows do not interrupt it

edits.before: Sion's E knocks back and shreds your magic resist before you have any Heat — no Danger Zone, no trade, just eat poke and farm.
edits.after: Roar of the Slayer knocks back minions, not you, and cuts armour rather than magic resist — level 1 the threat is poke, not shred.

edits.before: Full kit gives you the double Electro-Harpoon interrupt on his Q charge — the match is Skill because whoever respects the other's key ability wins the exchange.
edits.after: Your harpoons slow him but never interrupt a Decimating Smash charge — the match is Skill because it comes down to who steps out of the other's telegraph first.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Fully charged = knockup and stun, 10s at rank 1. Step out of the arc.

edits.before: Track Sion's Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged = knockup. Dodge it. When it is down — Flame + E-R him.
edits.after: Electro-Harpoon slows but never interrupts a Decimating Smash charge — walk out of the arc instead.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Liandry's Torment  (burn synergy), then Riftmaker; boots Sorcerer's Shoes. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Core: Liandry's Torment  (burn synergy), then Riftmaker; boots Sorcerer's Shoes. Anti-heal is for the zombie — Glory in Death heals him off every hit.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Decimating Smash: 10s at rank 1 — a slow will not interrupt the charge, so step out of the arc. - Soul Furnace: 15s, and its recast is max-health damage. - Roar of the Slayer: 12s, armour only. - Your R: kill windows only.

notes: The 'Electro-Harpoon interrupts his Q charge' instruction is the most dangerous single line I found across this slice — it tells the player to stand inside the Decimating Smash arc and throw slows at a charge that a slow cannot stop. It appears in wants.you[1], whys[2] and the content 'mid' paragraph; I fixed the first two, and the 'mid' paragraph still contains 'double-cast it the instant he starts the Q windup to interrupt his charge', which needs a whole-paragraph rewrite to fix inside the length band. Same for the content 'early' paragraph, which repeats the magic-resist-shred error. Standing note for Rumble: the kit file's knockup and terrain flags on Scrap Shield (W) are parsing misfires; Riot's description is a shield plus a movement-speed burst only. The existing text correctly notes Unstoppable Onslaught passes through an Equalizer zone — that is right, the Equalizer is a damage-and-slow zone rather than collidable terrain, despite the kit file's terrain flag on it.
